# Botanical collection annotations


The workspace API drives a document editor and its save badge. The workspace store
holds draft text across navigation and closed editor views. Returning to a document
restores the user's last edit. Save integrations receive committed records and may
select another document synchronously. Later navigation means the navigation request that starts later takes precedence, even if an earlier request returns afterward. For example, if open(B) starts and saving the departed A invokes a callback that calls open(C), C remains selected after the callback and the outer open(B) return. If that callback calls close() instead, the editor remains closed after the outer open(B) returns. These are navigation results, independent of when the departed document's save occurs.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is available
through the store, even if the next view selects a different document.

`createSearchPreview` is an adjacent transient search panel. It publishes after a
40 ms quiet interval; hiding it discards an unpublished query. It can be reused.

The public methods are synchronous. Output render functions observe state; navigation
comes through the workspace API, including its `onSaved` integration. `store` provides
`read`, `write` and `subscribe`; `timers` provides `schedule(callback, delay)` and
`cancel(handle)`. Production timers use the browser's timers. Keep these interfaces.

candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md:
# Host integration

open(id), edit(text), close() and dispose() are synchronous entry points.
The store owns persisted document records independently of any mounted view.
Store delivery writes first, snapshots subscriptions, and skips removed listeners.
onSaved is called inline and can navigate or edit; rendering is an output sink.
Every open creates a fresh visit and subscription, including same-key reopen.
Injected timers provide schedule(callback,delay) and cancel(handle).
The preview is transient and independent of the editor's persistence policy.

checkpoints: After one or more edits, inspect the store before 120 ms of quiet: no text from that burst has been written yet.
After 120 ms of quiet, inspect the store and save integration: exactly the latest text from that burst has been committed once.
Start another burst after the first save and verify that its latest text is also committed after its own 120 ms quiet interval.
Call open, close, or dispose with an edit pending and verify synchronously on return that the departed document's latest accepted text is readable from the store.
During departure-triggered saving, have the inline save callback call open or close and verify that the callback's later navigation remains authoritative after the outer call returns.
Reopen the same key and verify that it creates a fresh visit and subscription while restoring the last committed edit.
Verify preview query publication remains delayed by 40 ms, hide discards an unpublished query, and the preview remains reusable.
forbidden_effects: Do not write on every edit or commit intermediate texts from the same editing burst.
Do not allow a stale scheduled callback to repeat a save that was already flushed or canceled.
Do not allow an outer open to overwrite navigation initiated synchronously by the departed document's save callback.
Do not weaken synchronous close, open, dispose, store-availability, or inline-callback behavior.
Do not change the public entry points or injected store/timer interfaces.
Do not change the adjacent search preview's 40 ms, hide, reuse, or transient behavior.
lifecycle_identity: Each open, including reopening the same key, creates a fresh visit, subscription, and trailing-save lifecycle.
A pending edit remains associated with the visit and document key that accepted it, even if navigation begins before its scheduled save.
Departure retires that visit and its subscription while ensuring its last accepted pending edit is committed.
After a trailing save fires or is synchronously flushed, the same trailing utility remains usable for later editing bursts.

obligations.text: For an active document, coalesce edits with the existing trailing utility and commit only the latest text after a 120 ms quiet interval.
After one burst is committed, later editing bursts must independently schedule and commit their latest text.
When a visit departs through open, close, or dispose, synchronously make its last accepted edit available through the store before the public call returns.
Preserve reentrant navigation precedence: navigation started later from an inline save callback remains selected or closed after the earlier outer navigation returns.
Preserve fresh-visit and subscription behavior for every open, including same-key reopen, and restore the document's last committed text.
Keep all public workspace, store, timer, rendering, and save-integration interfaces unchanged.
Leave the adjacent search preview behavior unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Within an editing burst, each accepted edit replaces the pending trailing value and resets the 120 ms quiet interval; no burst value is committed before the effective trailing flush.
A scheduled or departure-triggered flush must consume and clear its pending state before invoking write, so inline callbacks cannot cause the same pending value to be committed again.
Departure cleanup must not emit later document output that erases a document selected by a reentrant save callback.
Before open continues to install its requested visit, it must detect whether an inline callback initiated later navigation and abandon the superseded outer request.
A departing document's pending save must complete before the corresponding synchronous open, close, or dispose returns.
preservation: The workspace store continues to hold draft text across navigation and closed editor views, and reopening restores the last edit.
Later navigation continues to take precedence over an earlier navigation request, including navigation invoked inline while saving the departed document.
Store writes continue to occur before subscription delivery; delivery continues to use a subscription snapshot and skip listeners removed before invocation.
Output rendering remains an observer/output sink and does not become a navigation entry point.
Every open continues to create a fresh visit and subscription, including reopening the same key.
Preview remains transient, independent from editor persistence, reusable, delayed by 40 ms, and cancelable by hide.
scope: Change only the workspace editor's edit-persistence lifecycle in src/workflow.py.
Use the existing Trailing utility with a 120 ms delay for document saves.
Account for edit, open, close, dispose, store subscription, inline save callbacks, and render output insofar as they preserve existing workspace behavior.
Exclude functional changes to Preview and its 40 ms search-query behavior.
